```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(sasonr)
```

## Run a SAS program

`sas_run()` takes SAS source code, runs it on the R engine and returns the
log, the listing and the WORK data sets.

```{r}
code <- "
data dm;
  input usubjid $ age sex $;
  datalines;
S01 45 M
S02 70 F
S03 .  F
;
run;

data adsl;
  set dm;
  length agegr1 $5;
  if missing(age) then agegr1 = 'Miss';
  else if age < 65 then agegr1 = '<65';
  else agegr1 = '>=65';
  put usubjid= age= agegr1=;
run;
"
res <- sas_run(code)
res$log
res$work$adsl
```

Missing values follow SAS rules: a missing numeric value is smaller than any
number, and character variables keep the length SAS would give them.

## See the generated R code

`sas_translate()` shows the R code that sasonr generates for each step. Simple
steps become vectorised `dplyr` pipelines; steps with cross-row state such as
`RETAIN`, `LAG` or `FIRST.`/`LAST.` use grouped vectorised code when the
result can be proven identical, and an explicit row loop otherwise.

```{r}
code2 <- "
data lab;
  input usubjid $ visit aval;
  datalines;
S01 1 10
S01 2 12
S02 1 20
S02 2 18
;
run;

data chg;
  set lab;
  by usubjid;
  retain base;
  if first.usubjid then base = aval;
  chg = aval - base;
run;
"
tr <- sas_translate(code2)
cat(tr$steps[[2]]$code)
sas_run(code2)$work$chg
```

## Macro language

Macro processing and execution interleave exactly as in SAS: a step is run
as soon as it is complete, so values created with `CALL SYMPUTX` are
available to the macro code that follows.

```{r}
code3 <- "
%macro check(ds);
  data _null_;
    call symputx('n', 3);
  run;
  %if &n > 2 %then %put NOTE: &ds is large;
  %else %put NOTE: &ds is small;
%mend check;
%check(adsl)
"
sas_run(code3)$log
```

## Unsupported features fail loudly

sasonr never guesses. A feature that has not been verified against SAS stops
the program with a classed condition that carries the SAS line number.

```{r, error = TRUE}
sas_run("data a; x = 1; run; proc report data=a; run;")
```
